policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV reads the plural, "tell thy servants the dream, and we will show the interpretation". The ketiv לעבדיך is the plural "thy servants"; the qere לְעַבְדָךְ is singular "thy servant". The English number distinguishes the ketiv. The two notes are an alternative rendering of "the Syrian language" and a scope note about the Aramaic section, and neither bears on this unit.

Qere לְכַשְׂדָּאֵי and ketiv לכשדיא are orthographic variants of the same gentilic plural; both are "to the Chaldeans", which is what ASV renders. Nothing in the wording distinguishes them, and the single note is an alternative_rendering of "The thing is gone from me", which cannot decide a reading.

Qere הִזְדְּמִנְתּוּן and ketiv הזמנתון differ only in whether the reflexive stem's assimilated dalet is written; both are the same 2mp verb rendered "ye have prepared". ASV shows no wording that separates them and the verse carries no note.
Qere כַשְׂדָּאֵי and ketiv כשדיא are spelling variants of the same word, rendered "Chaldean" either way. The note is an alternative_rendering of "no king, lord, or ruler" and never decides a reading.
Qere וּנְהוֹרָא and ketiv ונהירא are orthographic variants of the same noun, "and the light", which ASV renders with no feature separating them. No note attaches to the verse.
Qere הַאִיתָךְ and ketiv האיתיך differ only in the plene yod of the 2ms suffix; both are "art thou able". ASV's wording is identical under either and the verse has no note.

Qere מִנְּהֵין and ketiv מנהון differ only in the gender of the plural pronominal suffix. English "part of iron" marks no gender on the resumed antecedent, so ASV cannot distinguish them; the verse has no note.

Qere וּמִנְּהֵין and ketiv ומנהון differ only in suffix gender. ASV's "and part of clay" carries no gender for the suffix, so nothing in the English distinguishes the readings, and the verse has no note.
Qere דָיְרִין and ketiv דארין are orthographic variants of the same participle, "dwell". ASV renders one verb with nothing to separate the spellings, and the verse has no note.

Qere אֲרַע and ketiv ארעא differ in the state of the noun. ASV's "over all the earth" uses the article idiomatically after "all" in either case, so the English does not report the Aramaic state; the verse has no note.
Qere תְלִיתָאָה and ketiv תליתיא are spelling variants of the same ordinal, rendered "third" either way. Nothing in ASV distinguishes them and the verse has no note.
Qere רְבִיעָאָה and ketiv רביעיה are spelling variants of the same ordinal, rendered "the fourth" either way. ASV shows no feature that separates them and the verse has no note.

Qere מִנְּהֵן and ketiv מנהון differ only in suffix gender, which "part of potters' clay" does not express in English. The note is an alternative_rendering of "potters' clay" (Or, earthenware) and cannot decide a reading.

Qere וּמִנְּהֵין and ketiv ומנהון differ only in suffix gender; ASV's "and part of iron" marks none. The verse's only note is an alternative_rendering (Or, earthenware), which is about English wording.
Qere מִנְּהֵין and ketiv מנהון differ only in suffix gender, unexpressed in "part of iron". The note is an alternative_rendering of "broken" (Or, brittle) and never decides a reading.

Qere וּמִנְּהֵין and ketiv ומנהון differ only in suffix gender, which "and part of clay" does not express. The verse's note is an alternative_rendering (Or, brittle), which bears on English wording only.

The qere וְדִי carries the conjunctive waw and the ketiv די does not. ASV opens the clause "And whereas thou sawest the iron mixed with miry clay", rendering a conjunction that the ketiv has no basis for. The two notes are alternative renderings (Or, earthenware; Or, by) and do not bear on the conjunction.
